title: Multi-model bias of the global sea surface temperature climatology
science_question: How large is the 1971-2000 global sea surface temperature climatology bias of three CMIP6 historical simulations against the World Ocean Atlas 2023 observational climatology, and what is its spatial structure?
query:
Evaluate the 1971-2000 sea surface temperature (SST) climatology of three CMIP6 historical simulations against the World Ocean Atlas 2023 (WOA23) observational climatology, and describe the spatial structure of the bias.

Data to use:
- CMIP6 historical variable `tos` from CESM2, GFDL-ESM4 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR, monthly, from 1971-01 to 2000-12, each on its own native grid with its own published cell areas (areacello).
- WOA23 temperature, the 1971-2000 climate normal, annual time slice, objectively analysed field, at 0 m depth, on the 1-degree grid.
- The WOA23 1-degree land-sea mask (landsea_01), in which a cell is ocean when its value is greater than 1.

Follow this procedure exactly.

1. Model climatology. For each model, reduce the 360 monthly `tos` fields of the window to a single climatological field by taking their mean weighted by the length of each month in the model's own calendar. Do this on the model's own native grid; do not regrid at this stage. An unweighted mean over the time axis, which gives a 28-day February the same weight as a 31-day January, is not the answer.

2. Native global mean SST. For each model, report the area-weighted mean of its climatology over the whole of its own native ocean grid, weighting each cell by the model's published areacello. Report in degrees Celsius to 2 decimal places.

3. Observed global mean SST. Report the area-weighted mean of the WOA23 0 m annual field over the whole 1-degree grid, in degrees Celsius to 2 decimal places. Note in the answer that this and the three model values in step 2 are each taken over that product's own ocean mask, so they do not cover identical sets of cells.

4. Common comparison grid. Regrid each model's climatology conservatively onto the WOA23 1-degree grid. Then build ONE comparison mask and use the identical mask for all three models, so that the three models are scored on exactly the same sample of cells. A cell belongs to the mask when all of the following hold: the WOA23 land-sea mask marks it as ocean (value greater than 1); the WOA23 0 m annual field has a valid value there; and all three regridded model climatologies have a valid value there.

5. Bias and skill on the common mask. For each model, restricted to the common mask of step 4, report:
   - delta_SST, the area-weighted mean of (model minus WOA23), in degrees Celsius to 2 decimal places;
   - the area-weighted root-mean-square error against WOA23, in degrees Celsius to 3 decimal places;
   - the area-weighted spatial Pearson correlation coefficient between the model field and the WOA23 field, to 3 decimal places.
   Also report, for each model and for WOA23, the area-weighted mean over the common mask itself, so that delta_SST can be read as the difference of two means taken over the same cells.

6. Ranking. Rank the three models by the magnitude of delta_SST, from smallest absolute bias to largest, and state the ranking explicitly.

Produce two figures.

Figure 1, a 2-by-2 panel of global maps: three panels showing the bias field (model minus WOA23) of CESM2, GFDL-ESM4 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR on the common mask, all three drawn with one shared diverging colour scale centred on zero, and a fourth panel showing the WOA23 0 m reference SST field on the same mask with a sequential colour scale. Label every panel and give each colour scale a unit label in degrees Celsius.

Figure 2, a bar chart of the global mean SST from steps 2 and 3, with four bars labelled CESM2, GFDL-ESM4, MPI-ESM1-2-LR and WOA23. Annotate each bar with its value above the bar, and label the y axis in degrees Celsius.

expected_numeric_outputs.definition: area-weighted mean of the day-weighted 1971-2000 tos climatology over the model's own native ocean grid, weighted by the model's areacello
area-weighted mean of the WOA23 1971-2000 annual 0 m temperature over the whole 1-degree grid
area-weighted mean over the common comparison mask of step 4
area-weighted mean of (regridded model minus WOA23) over the common mask
area-weighted root-mean-square error against WOA23 over the common mask
area-weighted spatial Pearson correlation between the regridded model field and the WOA23 field over the common mask
the three models ordered from smallest to largest absolute delta_SST

expected_figures.content: three model bias fields on a shared zero-centred diverging scale, plus the WOA23 reference SST field
four bars (three models and WOA23) of the global mean SST of steps 2 and 3, each annotated with its value

grading_notes: The global means of step 2/3 are each over that product's own ocean mask; they are NOT the numbers delta_SST is built from. delta_SST is defined on the common mask of step 4 and equals the difference of the two common-mask means reported in step 5.
RMSE and the pattern correlation depend on the regridding method; the conservative method onto the WOA23 1-degree grid is prescribed, and an answer using another method should state which.
The comparison mask is shared by all three models on purpose, so the three RMSE values and the ranking rest on an identical sample of cells.

Reaching the model climatology as 30 day-weighted annual means and then averaging those 30 fields is an acceptable alternative route: it differs from the prescribed single day-weighted mean by less than 0.001 degC and changes none of the reported figures.

GFDL-ESM4's delta_SST of -0.0863 degC lies close to the -0.085 rounding boundary. Grade the 2-decimal value against the full-precision number in answer_T1.json rather than on the rounded string alone.
